article_title: Pre-Service Teachers' Perceptions of AI Technological Support and School-Based Intelligent Environment Support: Model-Based Indirect Associations with Innovative Competence via AI Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulated Learning
citation: Liu Xu, Zhang Meiqi, Du Jiaoyang. (2026). Pre-Service Teachers' Perceptions of AI Technological Support and School-Based Intelligent Environment Support: Model-Based Indirect Associations with Innovative Competence via AI Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulated Learning. Behavioral Sciences. https://doi.org/10.3390/bs16081378
title: 31-item five-scale questionnaire measuring AI support, mediators, and innovative competence
description: A 31-item Chinese questionnaire with five 5-point Likert scales: innovative competence (9 items across innovation willingness, readiness, and practice), self-regulated learning (5 items), AI self-efficacy (6 items), and combined AI technological support and school-based intelligent environment support (11 items). Items were adapted from prior instruments, reviewed by a six-expert panel, and translated and back-translated. Reliability was high: "the overall Cronbach's alpha coefficient of the questionnaire was 0.959, and the Cronbach's alpha coefficients of the five dimensions all exceeded 0.90"; CFA supported a five-factor model.
requirements: Administration with informed consent and validity screening (pre-survey control, in-survey monitoring, post-survey screening of invalid responses)
constraints: The measures capture perceived support rather than objectively verified technological provision or school-level conditions, as the article states
target_learners: Pre-service teachers in Chinese higher education institutions
target_learning_goals: Measuring perceived AI support, AI self-efficacy, self-regulated learning, and innovative competence
examples: Sample items include "I am willing to use AI to pioneer new teaching ideas" and "The intelligent education platform built by my school has rich learning resources"
key_sources: Liu Xu, Zhang Meiqi, Du Jiaoyang. (2026). Pre-Service Teachers' Perceptions of AI Technological Support and School-Based Intelligent Environment Support: Model-Based Indirect Associations with Innovative Competence via AI Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulated Learning. Behavioral Sciences. https://doi.org/10.3390/bs16081378

article_title: A Systematic Review of the Effects of Physical Activity on Specific Academic Skills of School Students
citation: Loturco, I.; Montoya, N.P.; Ferraz, M.B.; Berbat, V.; Pereira, L.A. (2022). A Systematic Review of the Effects of Physical Activity on Specific Academic Skills of School Students. Educ. Sci. 2022, 12, 134. https://doi.org/10.3390/educsci12020134
title: Corpus of 31 school-based physical activity intervention studies included in the meta-analysis
description: A set of 31 peer-reviewed studies identified through PubMed MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science searches following PRISMA guidelines, from which 24 used mathematics tests, 4 language tests, 10 reading assessments, and 9 composite scores. Intervention types comprised "increasing the volume of physical education classes, applying classroom-based activities in the regular school practices, promoting 'active' breaks between regular classes, and employing specific programs of 'active' lessons." Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool.
requirements: Included studies required quantitative pre- and post-intervention academic performance assessment and at least one physical activity intervention group with a comparison group
constraints: Studies assessing only acute effects, qualitative studies, and studies without full text or outcome data were excluded
target_learning_goals: Academic achievement in mathematics, language, reading, and composite measures
examples: Table 1 characterizes each study's country, participants, intervention, comparator, outcome measure, and overall risk of bias, with risks ranging from low risk to high risk
key_sources: Loturco, I.; Montoya, N.P.; Ferraz, M.B.; Berbat, V.; Pereira, L.A. (2022). A Systematic Review of the Effects of Physical Activity on Specific Academic Skills of School Students. Educ. Sci. 2022, 12, 134. https://doi.org/10.3390/educsci12020134

article_title: Doctoral physical therapy students’ increased confidence following exploration of active video gaming systems in a problem-based learning curriculum in the United States: a pre- and post-intervention study.
citation: Wormley Michelle Elizabeth, Romney Wendy, Veneri Diana, Oberlander Andrea. (2022). Doctoral physical therapy students' increased confidence following exploration of active video gaming systems in a problem-based learning curriculum in the United States: a pre- and post-intervention study. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2022.19.7
title: 31-item perceived-confidence survey adapted from Erlich and Russ-Eft with six AVG domains
description: A 31-question survey measuring DPT students' perceived confidence with AVG as a PT intervention, adapted from Erlich and Russ-Eft and administered via SurveyMonkey. "The 31-item survey included 3 demographic questions and assessed students' perceived confidence across 6 domains: general use of gaming (5 questions), game selection (7), plan of care (5), set-up (3), documentation (3), and setting (5). The internal consistency reliability of the current survey had a Cronbach's α of 0.97." Items were rated on a 0–100 confidence scale.
requirements: Administered before lab activity #1 and again 8 months later after lab activity #2
constraints: Measures self-perceived confidence, not actual knowledge or psychomotor performance
target_learning_goals: self-assessed confidence with active video gaming as a clinical intervention
examples: The post-test was completed at the end of lab activity #2, 8 months after the pre-test, after students' first 8-week clinical placement.
key_sources: Wormley Michelle Elizabeth, Romney Wendy, Veneri Diana, Oberlander Andrea. (2022). Doctoral physical therapy students' increased confidence following exploration of active video gaming systems in a problem-based learning curriculum in the United States: a pre- and post-intervention study. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2022.19.7
